characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: D/MAX-2500/PC diffractometer with Cu Kα X-ray tube; 2θ range 20°–100°, scanning speed 2° per min; specimen polished with #150–#800 sandpaper and ultrasonically cleaned with alcohol
characterization_methods.key_findings: As-cast 0Be pattern contains only austenite (γ) reflections; no ferrite δ or Be-compound peaks are labelled for 0Be
characterization_methods.purpose: determine the phase composition of the as-cast steels

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Axiovert 200 MAT; specimens etched with 8% nital (nitrate alcohol), surface finish 0.05 µm
characterization_methods.key_findings: 0Be shows a uniform, essentially single-phase austenite matrix with wavy light/dark cellular-dendritic etching contrast and scattered fine dark dots; no reticular or 'Chinese character' Be-Fe compounds are observed

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 500 gf load, 15×5 indentation matrix, average value of 25 points
characterization_methods.purpose: measure the microhardness of the as-cast matrix (austenite)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloys made from high-purity elements Fe (99.99%), Mn (99.99%), Al (99.99%), C (99.99%) and Be (99.99%) and melted into alloy ingots in a vacuum induction melting furnace under a high-purity argon atmosphere. The obtained ingot has a diameter of 60 mm and a thickness of 30 mm. This as-cast state corresponds to the pre-deformation ingot; no heat treatment or thermal deformation was applied to the as-cast sample.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness: 500 gf indentation load, 15×5 indentation matrix, average of 25 points. Density measured by Archimedes drainage with a high-precision balance (up to 0.01 g), average of three independent measurements.

phases_present.morphology: uniform, essentially single-phase austenite matrix with wavy light/dark dendritic (cellular) etching contrast and scattered fine dark dots

structures.overall_structure: As-cast 0Be Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C steel is completely austenitic: a single-phase austenite (γ) matrix with partial precipitates. No reticular or 'Chinese character' shaped Be–Fe compounds were observed. The as-cast XRD pattern of 0Be shows only austenite (γ) reflections (no ferrite δ or Be-compound peaks).

unmapped_findings: Nominal composition of the 0Be as-cast sample (wt%): Fe balance, Mn 30, Al 10, C 1.5, Be 0 (Table 1). Made from high-purity Fe (99.99%), Mn (99.99%), Al (99.99%), C (99.99%) and Be (99.99%).

DSC phase-transformation temperature for the Be-free 0Be alloy (heating after homogenisation): the text (b0035) quotes 1278.8 °C, whereas Fig. 6 prints a 0Be peak of 1320 °C (a broad peak rising from ≈1270 °C). This measurement is on the homogenised alloy rather than the as-cast state, so it is not attributed to the as-cast sample.

A calculated Fe–Be binary phase diagram (Fig. 19, thermodynamic/CALPHAD equilibrium) was used to rationalise Be solubility and compound formation (line compounds FeBe12 ≈ 0.13, FeBe5 ≈ 0.17, FeBe2 ≈ 0.33 mol fraction; liquidus peak just above 1400 °C). This is a thermodynamic calculation on the Fe–Be system, not a computation on the as-cast sample.
In the as-cast 0Be steel no reticular or 'Chinese character' shaped Be–Fe compounds were observed in the metallographic photographs, unlike the Be-bearing as-cast steels (b0030).
